nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Renewable energy certification|Clean energy credit rating_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What gaps in the literature does the paper address regarding Export Credit Agencies (ECAs)?
nodes.answer: The paper addresses the limited systematic analyses of ECA financial flows in the energy sector and the lack of scholarly work on the capacity of ECAs as distinct financial institutions in clean energy finance.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Renewable energy certification|Clean energy credit rating_qna_001
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the primary focus of the paper discussed in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The paper addresses gaps in the literature regarding the capacity of Export Credit Agencies (ECAs) to engage in clean energy finance and presents descriptive statistics of ECA investments from 2005 to 2023 for select G20 countries.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Renewable energy certification|Clean energy credit rating_qna_002
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What significant change was observed in the clean energy lending of the United Kingdom post-Paris agreement?
nodes.answer: The United Kingdom increased its annual clean energy lending from a pre-Paris average of $8.7 million USD to $64 million USD in the post-Paris period.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Renewable energy certification|Clean energy credit rating_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What general conclusion can be drawn about ECA investments in clean energy finance post-Paris Agreement based on the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The general conclusion is that despite some improvements, the growth in clean energy investments by ECAs remains minimal, with fossil fuel investments still being predominant.
